issues.description: Write path throws UnsupportedOperationException at runtime instead of being structurally absent
issues.detail: fieldsWriter throws at flush time rather than at config/construction. The format still accepts full writer parameters (confidenceInterval, bits, compress, mergeExec) only to fail later. Either split into a read-only base with a separate RW subclass (as tests already hint), or fail-fast at construction. Exception message should also name the replacement Lucene104 format.

issues.description: Public API symbols narrowed to package-private without a deprecation cycle
issues.detail: NAME, QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval, and the reader constructor go from public to package-private in one shot. Downstream users of Lucene99 scalar quantization get compile breaks on upgrade with no warning. Either keep them @Deprecated public for one release or document the break in CHANGES.txt under Backward Compatibility Breaks.

issues.description: @Deprecated annotation dropped from moved format classes
issues.detail: The classes were @Deprecated in core; after the move to backward_codecs the annotation is gone. Intent is still 'legacy, read-only, replaced by Lucene104,' and SPI-bound downstream code will silently rebind without compile-time warnings. Restore @Deprecated so javac/IDEs flag callers — package name alone is not an explicit signal.

issues.description: Patch bundles four orthogonal changes that should be separate commits
issues.detail: This single diff (1) moves files to backward_codecs, (2) tightens visibility on many symbols, (3) removes the writer path and unused mergeExec/numMergeWorkers fields, and (4) adds/renames RW test shims. Each is independently reviewable; bundled they are not, and bisecting a future regression becomes painful. Split into pure-move, visibility, and writer-removal patches.

issues.description: Protected fields demoted to package-private on a public abstract class with public subclasses
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues remains public and abstract, but previously-protected fields are now package-private. Same-package subclasses still compile, but out-of-package extension is silently foreclosed. Either mark the class final/sealed to make the no-extension contract explicit, or restore protected. Pick one — current state leaves the subclassing contract ambiguous.

issues.description: Dead numMergeWorkers/mergeExec constructor parameters still validated but discarded
issues.detail: Constructors continue to accept and validate numMergeWorkers and ExecutorService, but the fields were removed and values are silently dropped. Callers passing a real executor get no error and no effect. Either remove the now-meaningless validation, or keep @Deprecated overloads that document the no-op explicitly.

synthesis.summary: The relocation to backward_codecs is the right direction and mechanically sound, but the patch has shape problems. The panel agrees on three core defects: the writer path throws at runtime instead of being expressed in the type system, formerly-public symbols are narrowed without a deprecation cycle, and @Deprecated annotations were dropped from classes that are still legacy. Secondary concerns include dead constructor parameters that validate but discard inputs, and protected-to-package-private field demotions that leave the subclassing contract ambiguous. The PR should be split into separate move, visibility, and writer-removal commits before landing.
